2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. The petitioners have filed this writ petition with the following prayer:
"It is, therefore, most humbly and respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be graciously pleased to issue a Rule Nisi calling upon the O.P. to show cause as to why;
1. The O.P. No.2 shall not be directed to re-calculate the compensation on the basis of Rule 26 of the RFCTLA RR Act, 2013;
2. The Land Acquisition Collector, Sundargarh (O.P. No.-2) shall not be directed to refer the dispute raised under Annexure-3 series to the Ld. Court of Land Acquisition and Land Rehabilitation Authority U/s.64(1) of the RFCTLA RR Act, 2013."
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that through highlighting their grievance, the petitioners have filed representations vide Annexure-3 Series to the Writ Petition, but till date nothing has been done in the matter.
In such background, they pray that a direction be issued to Opposite Party No.2 to take a decision on the above noted petitions within a specific time period.

5. Considering the submissions made and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
this Court directs Opposite Party No.2 to take a decision on the above noted petitions in accordance Hemendra Kumar Mahanta And vs Collector-Cum-District Magistrate on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62184839/
1 with law and also keeping in view of Section-26 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation & Resettlement Act, 2013, within a period of three months from the date of production of certified copy of this order and communicate the result of such exercise to the petitioners.
6.
